rituals.name: PARK THE MEMORY FOR SUPPORTED CARE
rituals.title: PARK THE MEMORY FOR SUPPORTED CARE
rituals.ritual_name: PARK THE MEMORY FOR SUPPORTED CARE
rituals.goal: Stop reopening the memory and move it toward supported care; repair open gap.
rituals.steps:
1. Stop adding sensory detail or searching for meaning.
2. Choose a qualified professional or safe appointment for later support.
3. Say one short reminder that the topic needs supported care.
4. End the reminder without reopening the memory.
5. Return attention to a neutral task in the current environment.
rituals.winReward: The topic was parked for qualified support and attention settled on a neutral task in the present.
rituals.win: The topic was parked for qualified support and attention settled on a neutral task in the present.
rituals.mindBend: Some material becomes safer to process when containment is the skill, not deeper self-exploration.
rituals.formulaFlow: Stop Detail → Name Container → Name Reminder → Close Topic → Return Externally
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Keep your eyes open. Use only present-day room, date, place and support orientation. Do not revisit memories in detail, use trauma imagery, intensify sensations, or attempt unsupervised processing. Stop for flooding, feeling unreal or disconnected, or weakened orientation and connect with qualified human support.
This is grounding only, not trauma treatment.

rituals.name: BUILD A PRESENT-DAY SAFETY MAP
rituals.title: BUILD A PRESENT-DAY SAFETY MAP
rituals.goal: Reinforce useful link: build a short present-day safety map you can actually use.
rituals.steps:
1. Name two present-day supports that can actually be reached.
2. Name one familiar place where you feel more present and steady.
3. Identify a practical exit from the current stressful setting.
4. Choose the person or service to contact if steadiness drops.
5. Keep the short map in mind and avoid adding memory content.
rituals.winReward: You could name reachable support, a steadier place, an exit, and who to contact if needed.
rituals.win: You could name reachable support, a steadier place, an exit, and who to contact if needed.
rituals.mindBend: Safety feels more available when it is mapped as real people, places, and exits rather than left as an abstract hope.
rituals.formulaFlow: Name Supports → Mark Places → Name Options → Choose Contact → Hold Map

rituals.name: COUNT WHAT IS STILL HERE
rituals.title: COUNT WHAT IS STILL HERE
rituals.goal: Repair shared connection: break scarcity vision by seeing what is still available before deciding what is missing.
rituals.steps:
1. Name the shortage your mind is zoomed in on.
2. Find three resources already present: time, skill, support, money, options, or information.
3. Pick the one resource that can affect the problem now.
4. Use it once before searching for more.
rituals.winReward: The shortage stayed real, but one usable resource re-entered the picture and created a next move.
rituals.win: The shortage stayed real, but one usable resource re-entered the picture and created a next move.
rituals.mindBend: Scarcity narrows attention before it changes reality. Seeing what remains can restore options without pretending you already have enough.
rituals.formulaFlow: Name Shortage → Find Three → Choose Resource → Use It
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Stop if this turns into forced positivity or makes you ignore a real shortage that needs practical help.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.name: CLOSE THE MICRO-GAPS
rituals.title: CLOSE THE MICRO-GAPS
rituals.goal: Patch clear gap; shorten the delay between noticing distraction and returning to the anchor.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose an anchor and notice the precise moment contact breaks.
2. Instead of judging the distraction, shorten the delay before returning.
3. Track the interval between noticing and reconnection.
4. Let practice end after one stretch with visibly fewer or shorter gaps.
rituals.winReward: The gap from 'I wandered' to reconnection became visibly smaller during the practice.
rituals.win: The gap from 'I wandered' to reconnection became visibly smaller during the practice.
rituals.mindBend: A strong attention practice may improve recovery speed before it improves how often distraction happens.
rituals.formulaFlow: Choose Precise → Return Instead → Track Interval → Let Practice

PAUSE
Release focus if effort becomes rigid, painful, or compulsive.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.name: BREAK THE NIGHT'S STORYLINE
rituals.title: BREAK THE NIGHT'S STORYLINE
rituals.goal: Break a night-time storyline into unrelated images that cannot easily continue the plot — repair open seam.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose one harmless five-letter word, such as TABLE.
2. For the first letter, name a neutral thing beginning with it.
3. Picture it for about two seconds with no action, memory, or story.
4. Point to the next letter and a completely unrelated image. End after five letters.
rituals.winReward: Five letters produced five separate neutral images without becoming a connected story.
rituals.win: Five letters produced five separate neutral images without becoming a connected story.
rituals.mindBend: Narrative momentum needs continuity. Deliberately unrelated images remove the bridge the next scene normally walks across.
rituals.formulaFlow: Pick Word → Call Image → Flash Image → Jump Letter
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Use only while safely resting; never while driving. Stop if images become distressing, compulsive, or disorienting.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.name: THE ACTION HAD MANY AUTHORS
rituals.title: THE ACTION HAD MANY AUTHORS
rituals.goal: Stitch repairable break; see how your action was shaped by you and by the conditions around you.
rituals.steps:
1. Review one action. Name what shaped it: intention, habit, body, other people, resources, timing, culture, and chance.
2. Put yourself among those causes, not above them.
3. Keep responsibility for your part without claiming you caused everything.
rituals.winReward: Your part stayed accountable while the other causes of the action came back into view.
rituals.win: Your part stayed accountable while the other causes of the action came back into view.
rituals.mindBend: Responsibility does not mean you were the only cause. Seeing other causes can reduce both excessive blame and excessive pride.
rituals.formulaFlow: Name Conditions → Place Yourself → Keep Responsibility
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not scattered accountability for choices that caused harm.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.name: ALLY OR SABOTEUR?
rituals.title: ALLY OR SABOTEUR?
rituals.goal: Patch open gap; test whether a thought actually clarifies, protects, and leaves you more capable.
rituals.steps:
1. Ask the current thought three questions: Does it clarify the next move.
2. Does it protect something real.
3. Does it leave me more capable afterward.
4. Score each yes or no.
5. If it fails two, thank the warning and appoint a different inner adviser.
rituals.winReward: A thought that failed most of the test lost its advisory role without needing to be argued out of existence.
rituals.win: A thought that failed most of the test lost its advisory role without needing to be argued out of existence.
rituals.mindBend: Not every protective-sounding thought is useful counsel. Advice earns authority by what it helps you do afterward.
rituals.formulaFlow: Ask Thought → Check Protection → Leave Me → Score Yes → Thank Warning

rituals.name: STOP RENEWING THE CONSTRUCTION
rituals.title: STOP RENEWING THE CONSTRUCTION
rituals.goal: Stop refreshing one mental construction and let the existing residue fade by itself — repair needed boundary.
rituals.steps:
1. Spot the image, conclusion, or demand being refreshed.
2. For one minute, refuse only the renewal: no new scene, argument, or confirmation.
3. Let existing residue fade at its own rate.
4. Redirect the freed attention into a chosen sensory task.
rituals.winReward: No new scene, argument, or confirmation was added while attention moved into a chosen sensory task.
rituals.win: No new scene, argument, or confirmation was added while attention moved into a chosen sensory task.
rituals.mindBend: Some mental content persists because it is being repeatedly republished — ending the renewal is different from forcing the old copy away.
rituals.formulaFlow: Identify Image → Time → Let Existing → Redirect

rituals.name: PRECISE OUTSIDE, QUIET INSIDE
rituals.title: PRECISE OUTSIDE, QUIET INSIDE
rituals.goal: Do the required behaviour precisely while postponing the inner argument about it; mend open gap.
rituals.steps:
1. Set the exact external behaviour required.
2. Execute it with full timing and skill.
3. Meanwhile, decline the running argument about authorship, resentment, or imagined applause.
4. Allow the body to act while the inner courtroom stays closed until the task ends.
rituals.winReward: The external task reached completion before resentment, authorship, or imagined applause got a hearing.
rituals.win: The external task reached completion before resentment, authorship, or imagined applause got a hearing.
rituals.mindBend: Competent action does not require emotional agreement in the same second. The body can perform while the courtroom waits.
rituals.formulaFlow: Define → Execute → Imagine Applause → Let Body

rituals.name: NEXT PHYSICAL MOVEMENT
rituals.title: NEXT PHYSICAL MOVEMENT
rituals.goal: Repair one piece; find the first visible body movement that would mean the task has actually begun.
rituals.steps:
1. Ask what your body would visibly do first if the task began now.
2. Name the action and where it would happen in one short phrase.
3. Picture doing only that movement once.
4. Take that first movement before planning the remainder.

rituals.name: SOFT DELIVERY, SOLID MESSAGE
rituals.title: SOFT DELIVERY, SOLID MESSAGE
rituals.goal: Reconnect weak connection: keep the message firm while removing unnecessary attack from its delivery.
rituals.steps:
1. Remove attacks from your wording.
2. Show one sign of genuine interest, validate the understandable part of the other experience, and use an easy rather than contemptuous manner.
3. Keep your core message unchanged.
4. Gentleness edits delivery, not truth.
rituals.winReward: Interest, validation, and an easier manner changed the tone without changing the core truth.
rituals.win: Interest, validation, and an easier manner changed the tone without changing the core truth.

rituals.title: SAY IT IN YOUR MIND. DO NOT SEND IT.
rituals.ritual_name: SAY IT IN YOUR MIND. DO NOT SEND IT.
rituals.goal: Say the unsent truth in your mind, then leave contact alone for a full day — rejoin missing thread.
rituals.steps:
1. Imagine the person in front of you.
2. In your mind, say what happened, what you felt, what you needed, and what you now choose to release.
3. Let the message be honest, but do not plan harm.
4. Do not contact the person for twenty-four hours. Let the message stay only in your mind.

rituals.title: THE TWENTY-MINUTE TRUTH STORY
rituals.goal: Rebuild broken connection; tell the truth in a contained window and finish by returning to today.

rituals.title: LOOK FOR THE MISSING DANGER
rituals.goal: Look once for the sign that should be present if the feared model is right; reconnect missing piece.

1. Ask what sign must exist right now if the feared model is correct.
2. Search once, fairly.
3. If it is absent, keep that absence and reduce—not erase—the model’s weight.
4. Name the alternate explanation strengthened by the missing sign.

display.title: THREE ACTIVE FUTURES ONLY
display.goal: Reinforce working boundary: keep only three future possibilities active enough to affect the decision.
display.numberedSteps:

4. Decide from the three that remain.

rituals.name: VIVID IS NOT IMPORTANT
rituals.title: VIVID IS NOT IMPORTANT
rituals.goal: Separate how noticeable information feels from how much it actually changes the decision; mend shared connection.

rituals.title: STAMP THE ENDING INTO THE SENSES
rituals.ritual_name: STAMP THE ENDING INTO THE SENSES
rituals.goal: Mend working gap; give a truly finished topic one repeatable sensory ending and a clear return time.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose one finish you can repeat: wash your hands, hear a soft sound, touch a doorframe, or change the light.

rituals.title: RETURN EACH LOAD TO ITS SOURCE
rituals.ritual_name: RETURN EACH LOAD TO ITS SOURCE
rituals.goal: Stitch working piece; give each source of stress only the share of body alarm it actually contributed.
rituals.steps:
1. Name current stressors and estimate each contribution to body alarm.
2. Imagine arrows from the present feeling back to its actual sources.
3. Address the largest actionable contributor first; stop blaming the most visible issue for unrelated load.
rituals.winReward: The largest actionable source became clearer, and the most visible problem stopped carrying unrelated load.
rituals.win: The largest actionable source became clearer, and the most visible problem stopped carrying unrelated load.

rituals.name: CHANGE THE RHYTHM, CHANGE THE STATE
rituals.title: CHANGE THE RHYTHM, CHANGE THE STATE
rituals.ritual_name: CHANGE THE RHYTHM, CHANGE THE STATE
rituals.goal: Change the pace of speech, movement, or breathing and watch what emotional state follows; restore needed bridge.
rituals.steps:
1. Notice the cadence of speech, movement, or breathing.
2. Choose an opposite rhythm: agitated becomes deliberate, collapsed becomes lightly brisk, looping becomes irregular.
3. Maintain the new tempo through one simple task and observe the emotional shift.
rituals.winReward: One simple task was completed at a deliberately different rhythm, producing fresh information about the state.
rituals.win: One simple task was completed at a deliberately different rhythm, producing fresh information about the state.
rituals.mindBend: Emotion is partly carried in tempo. Changing cadence can alter what the body predicts before the story changes.
rituals.formulaFlow: Cadence → Choose Opposite → Observe Emotional

rituals.name: THEN, NOW, NEXT

4. Name the next ordinary thing you will do within ten minutes.

rituals.name: ENTER THROUGH A RANDOM DOOR
rituals.title: ENTER THROUGH A RANDOM DOOR
rituals.goal: Let a random workable section choose the starting point when order does not matter — patch working connection.
rituals.steps:
1. Name three to six task sections that can safely be done in any order and give each one a number.
2. Let the first number that pops into your mind choose the section. Do not pick again just because you dislike it.
3. Work only inside that section for ninety seconds; do not reorganise the whole project.
4. Notice one concrete sign of progress, then decide whether to choose another number or close.
rituals.winReward: Ninety seconds of real progress happened inside one section without reorganising the whole project first.
rituals.win: Ninety seconds of real progress happened inside one section without reorganising the whole project first.
rituals.mindBend: When several doors are equally valid, choosing can cost more energy than entering. Randomness can remove a decision that adds no value.

rituals.name: LEAVE A BRIDGE BACK
rituals.title: LEAVE A BRIDGE BACK
rituals.goal: Rebuild working bridge: leave the future version of you one exact phrase that points back into the task.
rituals.steps:
1. Before stopping, picture the exact next movement and current reasoning.
2. Hold one short phrase that tells you where to resume.
3. End the task without mentally reopening the whole plan.
4. On return, use the phrase and continue from that exact point.

rituals.title: CHOOSE THE EASIEST MISTAKE TO CATCH
rituals.ritual_name: CHOOSE THE EASIEST MISTAKE TO CATCH
rituals.goal: Prefer the option whose failure becomes visible while correction is still practical; repair small bridge.
rituals.steps:
1. Name the two or three live options. For each, picture the specific way it could fail—not a vague fear.
2. Name the earliest visible sign that failure has begun. It must be visible or clear, not a feeling alone.
3. State what corrective action would still be available when that sign appears and what cost has already accumulated.
4. Choose the option whose reliable warning arrives while correction is still practical. Use this as one decision criterion, not the whole verdict.

rituals.title: SORT THE SOUNDS BY DISTANCE
rituals.goal: Patch fresh break: use near, middle, and far sounds to reopen the sense of space around you.
rituals.steps:
1. Spot the nearest sound, one mid-distance sound, and the farthest audible layer.

rituals.name: HIDE THE OPTION NAMES
rituals.title: HIDE THE OPTION NAMES
rituals.goal: Compare options on relevant traits before reconnecting them to their emotionally loaded names; stitch broken connection.
rituals.steps:
1. In your mind, rename the leading options A, B, and C.
2. Pick three relevant traits such as time, fit, reliability, or learning.
3. Compare A, B, and C only on those traits without adding new arguments.
4. Reconnect each letter to its option and notice what truly changed the ranking.

1. Choose a simple sound or imagined shape.
2. Notice both its qualities and the act of perceiving at the same time.
3. Refuse to place all reality on either side.
4. Let seeing or hearing itself become primary for several seconds.
display.win: Sound or shape and the experience of knowing it stayed present together for several seconds.
display.mindBend: Perception is neither only the object nor only the observer. The live event happens in the relation between them.
display.formulaFlow: Choose Simple → Attend Time → Place Reality → Let Relationship

rituals.goal: Restore broken link; accept what already happened without turning acceptance into approval.
rituals.steps:
1. Name what happened without changing whether it was right or wrong.
2. Say, “Accepting that it happened is not approving it.”
3. Notice what energy is being spent fighting the fact that it already occurred.
4. Choose one boundary, repair, or next action that still belongs to you.

rituals.goal: Lower the panic load without testing your heart sensations or forcing your breathing; reconnect shared connection.

keywords: An unwanted thought feels meaningful because it appeared

display.title: NO SECRET MESSAGE
display.goal: Reinforce healthy boundary: let an intrusive thought exist without treating its arrival as a message.
display.numberedSteps:
1. Say, “A thought showed up.”
2. Add, “Showing up is not a message.”
3. Name one ordinary thing in front of you that has nothing to do with the thought.
4. Do that ordinary thing for ten seconds without checking whether the thought is gone.
display.win: The thought stayed unanswered while attention moved into an ordinary object and action unrelated to it.
display.mindBend: A thought's appearance tells you that the brain produced it. It does not automatically tell you why, what it means, or what deserves action.
display.formulaFlow: Name Arrival → Remove Message → Pick Ordinary → Continue Ten

safety.raw:
PAUSE
Stop if this makes you less steady, more distressed, or less able to act safely. Use human, professional, medical, or emergency support when the situation needs more than self-help.
This brief reset is not diagnosis, treatment, or emergency care.
